q: Are fabricated steel structures, towers and steel doors and windows covered by EU CBAM?
title: Are steel structures covered by CBAM?
short: Yes. Structures and parts of structures of iron or steel, such as bridges, towers, lattice masts, roof frames, columns, and steel doors, windows and frames, fall under heading 7308, which is in Annex I of the CBAM Regulation. Prefabricated buildings classified under 9406 are not covered today.
audience: Structural fabricators, tower makers and pre-engineered building suppliers exporting to the EU

ul: Bridges and bridge sections, lock gates, towers and lattice masts.
Roofs, roof frames, columns, pillars, scaffolding and shuttering props.
Doors, windows and their frames, and thresholds, of steel.
Plates, rods, angles, sections and tubes prepared for use in structures.
Prefabricated buildings shipped as a complete building, under 9406: not in Annex I today.
Plain sections, plates and beams not yet worked into structural parts: chapter 72, also covered.
Machinery frames classified with the machine under chapter 84: not covered.
Aluminium structures, doors and windows: heading 7610, covered as aluminium goods.

p: A fabricator cuts, drills, welds and paints steel bought from a mill. CBAM counts direct emissions of your own processes plus the embedded emissions of the steel you used as precursors. Cutting gases and paint shop ovens add a little; the mill's emissions per tonne decide most of your number. Ask each mill for its embedded emissions data now, by grade and route.

Embedded emissions per tonne of fabricated steel for the reporting period, the tonnes of each steel input and its supplier's figure, and your own fuel use. Without supplier data the importer falls back on default values, which include mark-ups from 2026.

The European Commission proposed in December 2025 to extend CBAM to certain downstream products made largely of steel and aluminium. As of October 2026 that proposal is not law. Until it is adopted, coverage is what Annex I lists today, so check Annex I again before each contract season.
